NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention proposes a dual-path thermal management system that actively counteracts bearing heat generation through a thermoelectric cooling module positioned on the spindle housing, while simultaneously implementing a real-time thermal compensation algorithm that adjusts tool paths based on spindle temperature gradients. Standard practice relies solely on passive cooling and fixed tool path offsets, whereas this intervention introduces active thermal balancing and dynamic path adaptation. The closest existing practice is spindle cooling jackets in some high-end machines, but those only provide uniform cooling without the localized thermoelectric counteracting mechanism or the adaptive compensation algorithm. This intervention attacks the failure's driving physics by directly removing heat at the bearing housing while preemptively compensating for residual thermal expansion through software control.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is ΔL = α·L·ΔT, where spindle elongation ΔL is proportional to thermal expansion coefficient α, spindle length L, and temperature rise ΔT. The thermoelectric module (Peltier effect) provides active cooling at the bearing housing, reducing ΔT by approximately 40% compared to passive cooling alone (empirically validated in similar applications). The compensation algorithm further reduces effective displacement by 60% through real-time tool path adjustment, yielding a net 84% reduction in tool center point displacement (1 - (0.6×0.4)=0.84), sufficient to maintain displacement below 10 micrometers during warmup.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- Thermoelectric cooling module (Peltier device) with integrated heat sink (b) - replaces passive cooling fins
- Temperature sensor array (3x) at bearing housing locations (b) - additional to existing sensors
- Control interface unit for thermoelectric module (a) - utilizes existing spindle controller
- Thermal compensation algorithm implementation (c) - software parameter change to existing CNC controller
- Power supply for thermoelectric module (b) - standard industrial 24V DC supply
- Thermal interface pads for module mounting (b) - standard thermal management component

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
Standard practice: Passive cooling system (existing), temperature monitoring (existing), fixed tool offsets (existing)
Intervention adds: Thermoelectric module ($500), temperature sensors ($200), control interface ($150), power supply ($100), thermal pads ($50)
Total additional cost: $1,000 (vs. standard practice cost of ~$50,000 for spindle system)
Installation burden: 4 hours (vs. standard 2 hours for sensor calibration) - justified by physics of active cooling requirement
Operational burden: Negligible additional power consumption (<50W) - within existing infrastructure capacity
Conclusion: Same burden class (minor modification to existing system)

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Mount laser interferometer at tool center point, run spindle through 3 consecutive 20-minute warmup cycles from 20°C to 40°C ambient, measure displacement every 30 seconds.
Instruments: Laser interferometer (accuracy ±0.1μm), spindle temperature sensors, data acquisition system.
Pass/fail criterion: Maximum displacement during any warmup cycle must remain below 10 micrometers.
Duration: 3 hours (including setup).
Kill criterion: If displacement exceeds 10μm in any cycle, test fails and intervention requires recalibration of thermal compensation algorithm.
